## 🎓 Today's lesson
**What is a Closing Auction Session (CAS) in stock markets?**
Most trading happens continuously throughout the day as buyers and sellers match prices. However, big institutional orders at the very end can cause sharp, artificial price swings. To prevent this, stock exchanges run a **Closing Auction Session (CAS)** during the last 15 to 30 minutes. During this window, orders accumulate without immediately executing. An algorithm then calculates the single price where the maximum volume of shares can trade. This single clearing price becomes the official daily closing price, preventing market manipulation. [[News On AIR]](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMioAFBVV95cUxQczc4Sm1HVEFYVF9oR2djUnRHMmdKaFdfanh1NmlNMTJ6RGdpODlfLWx4YTlGZExUQjhzOFdRQ0E2YVY0OGY4WE0xYVV5Wkx2djVpT2V4VDhtczVSQ3pwN05vWGNKdkJhLWM0OWhSMVRTRkxRanhoNUR1cGtucFBnM3lEZzdYTWs3R2c1N1JoWktIN05nMXYtcE1pSEpZWVls?oc=5)
